s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive low back and lower extremity pain with nighttime worsening in a pediatric patient
salient_findings: Progressively worsening low back pain and bilateral lower extremity pain
Intradural and extramedullary lesion at the L3 level on MRI
key_facts: 10-year-old boy
Two months of progressively worsening low back pain
Bilateral lower extremity pain
Pain worse at night and on waking
Difficulty bending at the waist
No sensory or motor deficits
No bladder or bowel dysfunction
Hyperdense lesion at the L3 level on lumbar spine CT
Intradural and extramedullary lesion on MRI
Lesion displaced the cauda equina ventrally
Faintly hyperintense on T1-weighted images
Hypointense on T2-weighted images
Uniform contrast enhancement without a dural tail sign
No additional lesions on MRI of the cervical, thoracic, and intracranial compartments

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Intradural and extramedullary lesion with uniform contrast enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Clear cell meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperdense lesion on CT and faintly hyperintense on T1-weighted images, consistent with meningioma subtype

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined lesion displacing the cauda equina ventrally, a common feature of schwannomas

shortlist.label: Myxopapillary ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intradural and extramedullary location, with hypointensity on T2-weighted images, consistent with ependymoma characteristics

shortlist.label: Neuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pediatric patient with progressive low back and lower extremity pain, a rare but possible diagnosis
